verdicts.title: Short Propositional Refutations for Dense Random 3CNF Formulas
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Random 3CNF formulas constitute an important distribution for measuring the average-case behavior of propositional proof systems. Lower bounds for random 3CNF refutations in many propositional proof systems are known. Most notably are the exponential-size resolution refutation lower bounds for random 3CNF formulas with $Ω(n^{1.5-ε}) $ clauses [Chvatal and Szemeredi (1988), Ben-Sasson and Wigderson (2001)]. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The cited paper discusses refutation lower bounds for random 3CNF formulas and the development of short refutations within Frege proof systems. However, it does not directly address the cumulative-entropy analogue of space lower bounds or provide a constant c>0 related to the balanced separator size |S|² as required by the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Abstraction and Acceleration in SMT-based Model-Checking for Array Programs
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Abstraction (in its various forms) is a powerful established technique in model-checking; still, when unbounded data-structures are concerned, it cannot always cope with divergence phenomena in a satisfactory way. Acceleration is an approach which is widely used to avoid divergence, but it has been applied mostly to integer programs. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses abstraction and acceleration techniques in SMT-based model-checking for array programs, focusing on handling complex formulas with nested quantifiers. This does not address the conjecture regarding Φ(π) >= c·|S|² for a constant c>0, which is related to resolution proof complexity and Tseitin formulas.

verdicts.title: On character formulas for simple and tilting modules
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We show that the characters of tilting modules can be used, in a concrete and explicit way, to obtain the simple characters of a connected reductive algebraic group $G$ over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic $p$, for all $p$.
